nodes.label: Neon
nodes.rationale: Neon is the brand and access path for a set of cloud backend primitives around Lakebase Postgres, not the name of the database. Agents pick it for instant Postgres provision, copy-on-write branches and snapshots, compute that scales to zero while storage is still billed, and ordinary Postgres that works with any driver or ORM. Keep a working Better Auth, Clerk, Supabase Auth, S3, or supplied DATABASE_URL unless the user asks to replace it. Prefer the CLI over the MCP server unless the CLI is unavailable, blocked, or unauthenticated.

nodes.label: Lakebase Postgres
nodes.rationale: The database itself, one product reached through Neon (free plan plus the other backend primitives) or through Databricks, with the same infrastructure, features, and engineering team. The lakebase architecture is OLTP directly on cloud object storage, with storage decoupled from compute. Every project ships with it. New projects are created in AWS regions, and application traffic should use a pooled DATABASE_URL. A supplied DATABASE_URL with no Neon credentials is schema work for the neon-postgres skill and should be finished without provisioning.

nodes.label: Neon Auth
nodes.rationale: Managed Better Auth with users and sessions stored in Postgres. Use the neon-auth skill when login, users, and sessions have no existing provider. Keep existing Better Auth, Clerk, or Supabase Auth unless the user asks to migrate; a Supabase Auth migration keeps SupabaseAuthAdapter call shapes. Auth cannot be enabled on a project that uses IP Allow or Private Networking. neon-auth is absent from the current CLI skill catalog, so do not run neon skills -s neon-auth. Selecting data-api also declares Auth because the default Data API provider requires it.

nodes.label: Object Storage
nodes.rationale: S3-compatible object storage that branches with the project. Keep an existing S3 or other object store unless the user asks to replace it. A public_read bucket can serve prototype pages, but there is no website mode (PutBucketWebsite returns 501), no SPA fallbacks, no custom domains, and no CDN, so every page view is egress. Available only in aws-us-east-2, aws-us-east-1, aws-eu-central-1, and aws-ap-southeast-1. Bucket setup lives in the neon-object-storage skill.

nodes.label: Neon Functions
nodes.rationale: Long-running serverless compute close to the database for WebSocket servers, server-sent events, APIs, and long agent HTTP streams. A function must start returning a response within 15 minutes, and a quiet stream must send at least one byte every 15 minutes. Public HTTPS URLs must verify a JWT or API key before accessing data. For long agent or image streams, mint a JWT on the app server and have the client call the function directly. New HTTP APIs belong here, or in an existing handler, rather than in browser-facing PostgREST. Same four AWS regions as Object Storage, the AI Gateway, and Realtime. Authentication and runtime limits are in the neon-functions skill.

nodes.label: AI Gateway
nodes.rationale: One API for frontier and open-source models, supporting chat completions and responses, powered by Databricks Unity AI Gateway. Declare aiGateway in neon.ts to request gateway env vars. Without neon.ts, a bare neon env pull includes the default gateway credential on claimed projects, but the implicit pulls inside link, checkout, and apply do not pull an undeclared gateway token. Same four AWS regions as Functions. Model routing is the neon-ai-gateway skill. On an unclaimed Claimable project the gateway is denied until a human claims it.

nodes.label: Realtime
nodes.rationale: Beta. Makes any SQL query live: type-safe live queries and optimistic mutations against Lakebase Postgres for reactive apps and agents. Declare it as preview.realtime in neon.ts. It is not available on a Claimable project until that project is claimed. Same four AWS regions as Functions. Setup, sealed queries, and client bindings are the neon-realtime skill.

nodes.label: Data API
nodes.rationale: Optional PostgREST-compatible HTTP interface. Use it only when the app already uses PostgREST or a supabase-js database client, or is migrating that client. There is no neon-data-api skill; configuration is dataApi in neon.ts. New apps should query Postgres from Functions or existing handlers. Putting PostgREST in the browser and relying on RLS is easy to get wrong because a misconfigured policy exposes the database. The default authProvider is neon, so enabling dataApi alone is a type error until Auth is enabled or authProvider is external with a JWKS URL. Do not enable Auth only to silence that error in an app that never needed the Data API. A Supabase package used only for Auth or Storage is not a database-client dependency. It is a compatibility toggle, not part of a default backend.

nodes.label: Neon Branch
nodes.rationale: An isolated copy-on-write clone of the data, taken from the current state or from a past state inside the project's retained history window. It shares data with its parent until writes diverge, and those writes are stored independently as deltas. It can be modified or deleted freely. Create one whenever you would create a git branch. neon checkout applies neon.ts only while creating a branch; checking out an existing branch does not reconcile it.

nodes.label: neon.ts
nodes.rationale: Branch config and infrastructure-as-code, written with defineConfig from @neon/config. It declares which services a branch should have and types the env vars those services imply. Empty functions or buckets maps are configuration slots, not a deployed API. Do not replace an existing neon.ts wholesale. Invalid combinations fail TypeScript compilation, and the error names the valid fix. neon deploy, an alias of neon config apply, provisions the declaration and then pulls env into the local env file. Never coerce a missing process.env value to an empty string: that uploads an empty value and deletes the live key. An empty KEY= assignment is also empty.

nodes.label: Claimable Neon
nodes.rationale: The no-account path, including neon.new, Claimable Postgres, claimable.neon.tech, instant Postgres, and a no-signup database. Do not create a Claimable project as a substitute when an existing account fails to authenticate; stop and ask the user to sign in. Do not run neon init --agent or neon auth on this path. Unclaimed projects expire at project_expires_at (72 hours today). Claim codes expire in expires_in (15 minutes today). Functions, Object Storage, and the AI Gateway report requires_claim until a human claims the project. Add Auth with neon.ts and neon deploy when login is requested and no existing provider should be kept.

nodes.label: Upstash Redis
nodes.rationale: Neon has no built-in key-value store. Pair it with Upstash Redis for caching hot reads and rate limits, and keep any Redis the app already uses.

nodes.label: Upstash QStash
nodes.rationale: Neon has no built-in message queue. Use Upstash QStash for background jobs, queues, retries, and delayed delivery to a Function, and keep any queue the app already uses. Cron and custom HTTP, WebSocket, or SSE work belong on Functions.

nodes.label: Databricks
nodes.rationale: The other way to reach the same Lakebase Postgres infrastructure, features, and engineering team, alongside the rest of the Databricks suite. Call the database Lakebase Postgres. Neon is the brand and the Neon access path.

nodes.label: Databricks Unity AI Gateway
nodes.rationale: The Databricks service that powers the Neon AI Gateway.

nodes.label: Neon CLI
nodes.rationale: Preferred over the MCP server because it can deploy Neon Functions and drive link, checkout, and neon.ts. Do not run neon login or neon auth unattended, and do not launch browser authentication for an unattended agent. Authenticated neon init writes neon.ts in place and does not deploy or wire the app. If init already installed the Neon plugin, do not also run neon mcp and neon skills for the same agent. link and checkout pull env by default; pass --no-env-pull when a supplied DATABASE_URL or AWS_* value must stay. init has no --no-env-pull flag.

nodes.label: Neon MCP Server
nodes.rationale: Fallback when the CLI is unavailable, blocked, unauthenticated, or the user prefers it. One global install serves every project. Without --oauth it writes an API key into the agent user config. A project-level install must use OAuth so no key lands in a file git can commit. Always pass --agent; with -y and no --agent, the command writes to every installed agent.

nodes.label: Better Auth
nodes.rationale: Keep a working Better Auth install. Neon Auth is the managed form; use it when there is no provider yet or the user asks to migrate login.

nodes.label: Clerk
nodes.rationale: Keep Clerk. Use neon-auth only if the user asks to migrate login.

nodes.label: Supabase Auth
nodes.rationale: Keep Supabase Auth unless the user asks to migrate. A migration uses Managed Better Auth and keeps SupabaseAuthAdapter call shapes. A Supabase package used only for Auth or Storage does not establish a database-client dependency.

nodes.label: PostgREST
nodes.rationale: The Data API is the compatibility path for an existing PostgREST client or a supabase-js database client. Browser PostgREST with RLS is a poor fit for a new app because a bad policy exposes the database. Generic REST endpoints should be a Function or an existing handler.

nodes.label: Branch-First Dev Flow
nodes.rationale: Recommended day-to-day loop when using Neon services. neon.ts declares what every branch should have, and checkout is how you move between those branches. Each half works on its own, and they compose. link and checkout pull the branch env by default, so DATABASE_URL lands in the local env file. Pass --no-env-pull and use neon-env run, neon-env export, fetchEnv, or neon dev when secrets should not be written to disk. Checking out an existing branch does not apply neon.ts; use neon deploy --env for that.

nodes.label: Neon Agent Program
nodes.rationale: Enroll only when the work is a fleet of user databases, such as app-generating agents and platforms. A single-app backend skips this. The program page covers instant provision, snapshots, scale-to-zero compute with storage still billed, Auth, and Data API compatibility. Guidance for platforms that operate Lakebase Postgres on Neon at scale is the neon-postgres-agent-platforms skill in the separate neondatabase/neon-for-agent-platforms repo.

nodes.label: S3
nodes.rationale: Keep a working S3 or other object store. Neon Object Storage is the S3-compatible choice when the app has no object store yet.
